The *Cetanālakkhaṇapañha* ("The Question on the Mark of Intention", Mil 3.3.11) is a section of the *Milindapañha* that addresses the defining characteristic or mark of intention (*cetanā*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations include an English rendering by John Kelly, alongside versions in other languages [SuttaCentral].

A full parallel to the dialogue is preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon under the title *The Characteristics of Thought* (T 1670b 2.33) [SuttaCentral]. While DharmaNexus reports no automated cross-language alignments meeting its threshold, it identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse comprising 123 matching passages across 18 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse correspondences occur with canonical discourses including the *Cūḷakammavibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 135), the *Moggallāna Saṁyutta* (SN 40), the *Sattakanipāta* (AN 7), the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), and the *Kosala Saṁyutta* (SN 3) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares formulaic framing with internal *Milindapañha* dialogues such as the *Vedanālakkhaṇapañha* (Mil 3.3.9) and the *Nāmarūpaekattanānattapañha* (Mil 3.2.6), as well as passages from the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), the *Mahāsīhanāda Sutta* (MN 12), the *Sāleyyaka Sutta* (MN 41), and several other sections of the Nikāyas [DharmaNexus].
